summary: Clarifies how IPv6 addresses are written in the Session Description Protocol. It was replaced by RFC 4566.

eli5.summary: The newer, longer kind of Internet address needed clear rules for being written in session descriptions. It has been replaced by RFC 4566.

subtitle: Rules for writing IPv6 addresses in session descriptions

tldr.problem: Session Description Protocol had rules for IPv4 addresses but left IPv6 syntax undefined, creating ambiguity.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3266 clarifies the ABNF grammar for IPv6 addresses in SDP by referencing the standard IPv6 text representation formats from RFCs 2373 and 2732.
tldr.outcome: Replaced by RFC 4566, this update ensured SDP could unambiguously describe multimedia sessions using IPv6.

today: RFC 3266 was replaced by RFC 4566. It remains a Proposed Standard for IPv6 address syntax in SDP.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: Session Description Protocol (SDP) is text format for describing multimedia sessions with details like the originator, media type, connection address, and attributes. It had defined the syntax for IPv4 addresses but not IPv6. The grammar definition for IP addresses left IPv6 undefined, causing uncertainty about how to write longer addresses in SDP.
sections.eli5: When you want to describe a video call or audio stream online, you write the address of where it is. The rules were clear for old-style addresses but not for new ones.

sections.title: IPv6 Syntax in SDP
sections.content: RFC 3266 updates the ABNF grammar to include IPv6 addresses by citing the standard IPv6 text representation from RFC 2373, with the special URL format from RFC 2732. The address type "IP6" is now allowed in the connection field (c=) of SDP, and both unicast and multicast IPv6 addresses are supported. An IPv6 address in SDP follows the same format used in URLs and domain names.
sections.eli5: Now you can write the long addresses in the same format you use on the web. The document shows what that format is.

sections.title: Example and Notes
sections.content: An example SDP session shows the origin and connection fields with IPv6 addresses. Implementors should note that IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (which represent IPv4 nodes) should be treated as IPv4 addresses, not IPv6.
sections.eli5: Here is what it looks like in real session descriptions, and a note for programmers about a special case.
